title: Clive L. Dragoon
dek: A wary escort whose determination to stop the raiders complicates a moment when negotiation might resume.

facts.Dispute: Trust and force during a parley
facts.Status: Travels with the caravan company; the later meeting is unrecorded

sources: Quest RP refreshed source · supplied 23 October 2026 · 3,845 messages across the main channel and two accessible threads; posting chronology and narrated continuations remain distinct
body:
Clive joins Vessalia, Thorn and Velkyn on the grain caravan. His caution about the attackers remains part of the encounter, alongside the consequences of using force while others try to talk.

Protecting the caravan

He questions the merchant about the attacks and tells a rider to shelter if wounded, offering to drive. He also objects when Papirak is referred to disrespectfully. These are actions and reactions in the scene, not a complete earlier history.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3.

A mistimed attack

When the slasher realizes he faces adventurers and becomes willing to listen, Clive attacks his mind while demanding surrender. The narrator explicitly says this spoils that opening for peace. Vessalia later restores a conversation through persuasion and healing, then silences Clive while negotiating.

The outcome is neither proof that caution was needless nor that negotiation was impossible. The party still obtains a conditional pause in raids.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

A risk left open

Clive asks whether the proposed meeting could be a trap and points to the wounds the raiders inflicted. The source closes before the meeting with the First Hunter. Its safety, the caravan’s later delivery and any lasting settlement remain unknown.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3.

What service should ask of a person

Clive brings stone to Ryvyting Creations and speaks with Farkur about his fear of losing control in a fight. His account of his powers remains personal testimony. Farkur urges preparation and service, without demonstrating that the feared loss of control has occurred.

Later, Pell challenges Clive’s assumption that earlier arrivals can expect a newcomer to fight. Pell insists on being asked and being able to choose. Their disagreement does not create a compulsory rule of the Gate. Clive also helps Pell practice with weapons and later takes up cleaning at the bathhouse: his own service includes work away from combat.
